answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, limiting how far influence can travel without repeated, independent links. A Sybil cluster—even one whose identities are named tide, pigment, and sable—typically connects to honest participants through a sparse external cut. Its low conductance constrains walk leakage; min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore limit the cluster’s aggregate voting weight rather than treating its many identities as independent trust.
